title: Backcasting from 'Security vs Innovation Framing Doesn't Hide Capitulation': Content-Analyzing AISI/CAISI Communications

original_idea.body:
# Backcasting from 'Security vs Innovation Framing Doesn't Hide Capitulation': Content-Analyzing AISI/CAISI Communications

**Problem:** A success state where national AI institutes coordinate effectively requires understanding whether divergent framings (UK 'AI Security Institute' vs US 'CAISI' innovation framing) reflect real policy divergence or just branding. We lack a systematic comparison of what these bodies actually prioritize.

**Direction:** Collect public documents from UK AISI, US CAISI/NIST, and 2-3 other national institutes (blog posts, frameworks, eval reports). Build a coded content analysis: frequency of safety vs capability vs economic terms, topics evaluated, binding vs voluntary language. Use simple NLP (keyword/topic counts, sentiment, an LLM-coded topic taxonomy with a fixed rubric) to quantify framing divergence and overlap.

**Why it matters:** Backcasting from 'effective international coordination' shows the precondition is shared substantive priorities, not just shared labels. Quantifying whether 'security vs innovation' is rhetoric or real divergence directly follows up the surprising AISI/CAISI renaming result and informs the International Network of AI Safety Institutes. Public-document analysis, no lab access needed.

**Relevant context:** Subfield surprising result: UK AISI renamed 'AI Security Institute', US AISI renamed CAISI (innovation framing). International Network of AI Safety Institutes; MIRI 2025 governance agenda on strategic landscape.
